recentItems.title: EU-Canada partnership: Talks in Montreal as both sides seek closer ties
recentItems.description:
The European Union and Canada are holding talks in Montreal on a first-of-its-kind partnership.

Brussels says the agreement could bring Canada closer to the EU than ever before, as both sides seek to reduce their reliance on the US.

Last month, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen suggested Canada could become the EU’s first “associate member”, a proposal that has sparked political debate.

Al Jazeera’s Rosie Birchard reports from Brussels.

recentItems.title: Syria flash floods: At least five killed and five others missing
recentItems.description:
Heavy flash floods and thunderstorms in Syria have left at least five people dead, including four children.

Search operations are continuing for five people still missing, while at least 25 others have been rescued.

Al Jazeera’s Heidi Pett reports from Damascus.

recentItems.title: Ukraine launches massive drone attack on Moscow, Russian oil refinery reportedly hit
recentItems.description:
Ukraine launched one of its largest overnight drone attacks on Moscow this year, forcing airports to suspend flights as Russian air defences intercepted incoming drones.

Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin reported more than 860 Ukrainian drones heading towards the region, with hundreds intercepted.

In Russia’s Samara region, Ukrainian drones reportedly struck the Novokuybyshevsk oil refinery, although Russian authorities have not confirmed the strike. A military food supply facility in Bryansk was also reportedly targeted.

Al Jazeera’s Yulia Shapovalova reports from Moscow on the attacks and disruptions across Russia.

recentItems.title: Sudan's paramilitary Rapid Support Forces: New wave of defections signals internal divisions
recentItems.description:
A new wave of defections is raising questions about growing divisions within Sudan’s paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF).

The latest defector is Major General Siddiq Abdelrahman Ander, an RSF commander who announced his departure in an exclusive video obtained by Al Jazeera English.

But what’s driving these defections as Sudan’s years-long war continues?

Al Jazeera’s Almigdad Alruhaid reports from Khartoum.

recentItems.title: Fighting in southern Ethiopia: Tens of thousands flee to Kenya
recentItems.description:
Tens of thousands of people have fled southern Ethiopia into neighbouring Kenya as fighting intensifies between forces from Ethiopia’s Oromia and Somali regions over control of the border town of Moyale.

Thousands of displaced people are sheltering in a school on the Kenyan side of the town, having escaped the violence across the border.

Aid agencies warn that food, water and shelter are running short as growing numbers of people seek safety.

Al Jazeera’s Malcolm Webb reports from Moyale, Kenya, where families are struggling to access basic necessities after fleeing the fighting.
